newsitem.title: CHINA: New technology saves China grain in liquor output.
newsitem.headline: New technology saves China grain in liquor output.

text.p: China has introduced a new distilling method which enables producers to save an average of 500 kg of grain per tonne of liquor, an official of the Chinese General Association of Light Industry said on Tuesday.
About 70 percent of China's big distillers have adopted the new technology that uses alcohol-active dry yeast, he said.
The new method also saves an average of 50 tonnes of water and 12 kilowatts of electricity per tonne of spirits, the official said.
China's distilleries producing popular high-alcohol spirits consume about 14 million tonnes of grain a year. China's grain harvet last year was 490 million tonnes.
China is trying to cut production of grain-based spirits in favour of fruit-based wines and beer to cut the industry's grain consumption.
China produced about 6.5 million tonnes of grain-based spirits in 1996.
